speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: This year, we commemorate 55 years of National Service (NS).

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Singapore remains one of the few countries where NS enjoys high levels of public support.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Well, every year, we take polls, similar to other questions asked by other Government agencies.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There are very few questions that you can get above 85%, let alone 90% or 95%.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Today, more than one million have served NS.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Each year, every young male citizen and Permanent Resident (PR) puts his personal commitment into action by enlisting into SAF or Home Team for full-time NS.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have had this high support of NS for many years now and I want to make clear to Members of this House that this strong support that Singapore enjoys is an exception and not the norm, compared to other countries with military conscription.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If you study the global landscape of countries that have mandatory national service, compared to when we first started it 50-odd years ago, the list of countries has shrunk significantly.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I have spoken in this House about the Baltic states which gave up national service, only to wish today that they did not.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But not only in terms of just countries that have managed to keep their national service, but many countries were forced to cut their national service commitments for a variety of negative reasons.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, it would be a serious mistake if we take that affirmation we receive today from Singaporeans for NS, that we take it for granted, or think it came by happenstance.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: At its core, it means that all male Singaporeans and PRs who are fit and liable to serve, are conscripted for full-time National Service, as required by the Enlistment Act and not at a time of their choosing.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Further, during the two years that they serve NS, all personal goals are put aside and placed subservient to the higher duty to defend Singapore.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Juxtapose that with those who ask for deferment, disruption, to come at a time of their choosing and to pursue their personal goals if they have sporting or arts talents.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We can only understand it because we apply very strict enforcement while, on the other hand, to those who must enlist for NS, we provide deferments and disruptions for any reason, sparingly, justified adequately and implemented openly.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If you are so harsh, as the main core of your policy, then you have to be very, very careful that your disruptions and deferments are sparing, justified openly and adequately.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Each appeal for deferment and disruption from sports and arts talent must, therefore, pass a very high bar.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Each request is assessed on its own merit, in consultation with MCCY, taking into consideration the applicant's past achievements and potential to excel in international competitions and bring national glory.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We allow deferments and disruptions for arts and sports talents when there is a higher goal of national glory.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But this deferment or disruption is not a licence to do away with your NS obligations.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, even when granted, there is no abdication of NS duties.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And we have to ensure that the applicant's NS duties are taken seriously and that he must be trained to be competent in his assigned vocation.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: This will include periods like BMT, specialists and commanders' courses, and his unit's key operations, which the applicant must fulfil as part of his NS duties, even if he is granted deferment and disruption.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Now, even with these strict criteria, I must inform the House that not all Singaporeans support deferment or disruption for sportsmen.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I quote a letter published in The Straits Times in May of this year, quote: "Let us not set the precedent by letting individuals call for a dialogue for the benefit of a privileged few.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Medals can bring glory to Singapore but it is more important to have people with commitment to serve National Service for Singapore's peace and security.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: All Singaporean sportsmen should know that if there is no Singapore, there is no sport to talk about." I leave you to decide whether you agree with the views.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I am quoting to tell you that there are Singaporeans, even despite the strict application of deferments and disruptions, do not agree with it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: MINDEF also receives letters from Singaporeans from time to time, questioning the fairness when deferred sportsmen receive financial rewards through endorsements, while others had to serve their NS as required.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They asked if this was compatible with the assurance given that deferments or disruptions should not be for personal gain, but national glory.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I cite these criticisms to show that even when sparingly applied, deferments and disruptions can have a pernicious effect – to cause invidious comparisons that some are given preferential treatment and are not performing their NS duties.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: MINDEF reiterates that all NS men must perform their duties, and their short-term disruptions or leave for sportsmen to train for and compete in international competitions are only allowed outside critical NS periods.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And those who have benefited from these provisions in the most recent SEA Games include paddler CPL (NS) Koen Pang, hurdler CPT (Dr) Ang Chen Xiang and triathlete OCT Luke Chua, apart from the swimmers that you have read about.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: From time to time, MINDEF convenes review committees to address these and other NS issues as top-down initiatives.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And you will remember that the last NS Review Committee was just held and completed from 2020 to 2022.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And I have reported on the recommendations of that review and the implementation to this House.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But there is also space for ground-up dialogues.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: After 55 years, I think we do have strong agreement on the common principles of NS – which is, everyone, regardless of talent or status, must fulfil their NS obligations as a first priority and all personal pursuits must be secondary to this during their full-time NS.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And based on this understanding, for sporting talents who bring national glory to Singapore, we can and have allowed limited deferments and disruptions, but without compromising their NS obligations.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I am proud that our national athletes understand and accept this duty of NS.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: None of them has asked to be exempted from NS duties, including those who trained hard and participated in recent regional and international events.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They understand that everyone must fulfil their NS duties, even if you are a sporting or art talent.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I also know that our national sportsmen want to do well in both – fulfil their NS duties and also win medals for Singapore; at least some of them.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: This is on the understanding that they fulfil the full period required after their disruption and also perform their NS duties satisfactorily while in NS.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, first of all, I thank the Minister for the clarification.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But I think based on the reaction and feedback of the athletes recently that we read in the papers, there seems to be still insufficient leeway given.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just now, the Minister did mention a little bit about —

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I suggest he does not make another speech.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, can you just ask your question?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Okay, can I ask the Minister again to confirm that he will look into further relaxation for athletes who want to perform better in their —

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And I think my answer speaks for itself.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, do you wish to ask the question?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: My second question is: while the Minister has said that personal development should be secondary to National Service, I think as our society becomes more sophisticated, there is also a need —

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Is this a further point or a clarification?

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: He is asking a question, so let him do it.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, there is also a need for us to give more room for our talents to develop.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And the situation we have now today —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Yes, we have a situation now today, that while we are hindering the development of our sports and arts talents by not granting them enough deferment in some cases, there are also a lot of citizens by registration that are not performing —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I am going to ask you one more time.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Well, you are making a lot of statements.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I have not heard a question from you.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Okay, so, let me ask the question again.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: — that citizens by registration are not doing their National Service.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I think he has filed a separate question and I think he can read the reply.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: No, I asked a question and the Minister said that he is not answering the question.
